title: Normalized whole-system reduction tensor presentation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with integers $O$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the completed-coefficient module categories and scalar restriction [def-sf-scalar-reduction-categories-restriction]. On each small pro-etale site use the actual $\ell$-power coefficient tower [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], its abelian presentation [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and its normalized derived reduction [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]. Use the vertical ringed sequence topology [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] and its generic strict semilinear systems [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Transport that presentation by the section-preserving strict-system/sequence-site equivalence [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]; write $r_T$ for the transported reduction and $L_T$ for its total derived inverse limit, with the normalized adjunction [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Given the recorded ordinary integral tensor model [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge], its flat-term K-flat pro-etale presentation [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model], the ringed total-tensor representative model [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], and section-model system tensor calculus [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus], a normalized tensor-reduction presentation consists of a derived natural isomorphism $\mu:r_T(-\otimes^L-)\cong r_T(-)\otimes^Lr_T(-)$ together with an ordinary strict-complex tensor isomorphism. On every total summand its forward map sends the actual quotient augmentation of $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the actual quotient augmentations of $x,y$. Ordinary reduction takes flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex] to K-flat complexes on the whole sequence site; the derived comparison is the localization of that strict-complex map, using the recorded reduction counits and the two tensor representative comparisons. This is a presentation of maps and their specified normalization, not an assertion of their existence.
